<a id="command-line-reference"></a>

# Command-Line Reference

Global behavior: JSON output by default, `--text` for a human summary, `--dry-run` for mutations, stable error codes on stderr and exit code 0 on success. `pecia help <command>` is the authoritative flag reference.

`book`: `new`, `open`, `close`, `status`, `move`, `rename`, `unregister`, `purge` and `set`. A library is created with `new --library`; `set` changes the output mode, the contents list, numbering, the index depth, the language or a `library.*` README slot. Book IDs and output paths are case-insensitively unique, and reserved store names and Windows alias forms are rejected. `book new` refuses a non-empty store directory for an ID, so run `book purge` before reusing an ID. `book new --force` renders into a non-empty output directory and backs up each foreign output file as `<name>.bak` before writing. `book purge` deletes the working data of an unregistered book: its store directory, rollback pool, lock files and temp inputs. It never touches the rendered output and refuses a registered, open or library book. `book unregister --purge` removes the registry entry and that working data in one invocation; without the flag only the entry is removed. The setting keys are `output` (`monolith`, `chapter`, `part`), `toc` (`on`/`off`), `numbering` (`on`/`off`), `index-depth` (an integer), `language` (a language code such as `de-DE`) and the library layout keys `library.slots`, `library.navigation`, `library.badges`, `library.footer`, `library.documentIndex`, `library.<slot>.heading|title` and `library.index.columns|shape`.

Structure: `add`, `move`, `remove`, `rename` and `block type`. Placement uses `--child-of`, `--index`, `--before` and `--after`.

Bodies: `body set`, `body append`, `body prepend`, `body get`, `body list` and `body replace`. Block `0` creates a body under the parent. `--file` and stdin accept UTF-8 with or without a byte-order mark, and UTF-16 or UTF-32 with a byte-order mark; an input that cannot be decoded is refused with `text.invalid-encoding`.

Editorial: `prose`, `region`, `status`, `badge`, `layout` and `asciiui`. All are open-only and dry-run aware.

Grammar: `grammar check` (with `--require-check` to fail on an incomplete check and `--language` for raw or file checks), `grammar apply`, `grammar languages` and the server lifecycle commands; `terms` manages the pending and confirmed term layers and `terms check` tests a candidate against the server. The grammar keys are `grammar.endpoint`, `grammar.policy`, `grammar.timeout` and `grammar.language`, and `grammar server-info` reports the effective interval, its cap and the supported set.

Render and inspect: `sync` renders, `check` reports findings and `verify` runs the acceptance view. `library sync` renders every registered book.

Read-only helpers: `find` searches titles, bodies, layouts and regions across one book or the whole library with modes, fields, metadata filters, grouping and four result shapes; `index` builds, inspects or clears the derived search index; `migrate status` and `migrate plan` report and plan schema migrations; `flush` lists or removes stale transient inputs; `rollback list` and `rollback restore` manage the undo packages.

Project helpers: `config`, `library defaults`, `version` and `help`. The `badge` group declares and checks badges, and its detectors live in `clabok.json`. `dump` and `restore` move a container, while `export` and `import` move the text form. `serve` starts the optional coordinator daemon used by the daemon concurrency mode.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failure, 2 usage and 3 rejected. The JSON envelope carries `schema`, `ok`, `command` and either `data` or `error` with a stable code, a message and an optional hint and details.

`apply` executes a declarative JSON plan against an open book under one lock and one rollback point. Plan version 1 supports `add`, optionally with `text` for a newly created block, plus `rename`, `move`, `remove`, `type`, `setting` and `body`, which sets an existing placed block. Every body text passes the grammar gate, and a failing step leaves the book unchanged.

```json
{"version": 1, "steps": [
  {"op": "add", "title": "Getting Started", "text": "Hello from CLABOK."},
  {"op": "setting", "key": "numbering", "value": "on"}
]}
```
